raw_response:
Let me step into this farmer's identity and reason through her decisions.

---

*Thinking as this farmer...*

Alright. Seven mu. I've been working this land for thirty years, so I know what it does and doesn't do. Four mu I keep in wheat and maize — plant wheat in the fall, harvest early June, turn it around fast for maize. The other three mu I put in cotton. My neighbor Mrs. Zhang dropped her cotton last year and went all wheat-maize, but I'm not ready to do that yet. Cotton money comes later in the season, and it helps when the maize price isn't good.

My husband does some construction work off-farm during the winter and spring, which means I'm doing most of the wheat management myself, and my son helps when he's home. By summer he's usually back for the busy maize season. For cotton picking in September, I'll need to hire a few people — my back can't do all of it anymore and my daughter-in-law has the baby.

**Wheat (4 mu):** I'll plant early October, same as always. I go with the Jimai 22 variety — the village supply shop has it and my neighbor gets decent yields with it. For fertilizer, I put down a compound bag as base before plowing, probably a 50-kg bag of the 18-46-0 type for the four mu, plus some potash. At jointing stage — usually late February or early March — I'll topdress with urea, about half a bag per mu. The extension person once told me I should do a soil test, but honestly I've been doing this so long I can tell by how the leaves look whether I need more nitrogen. I'll water three times: once before winter to help the roots set, once at jointing, once at grain fill. If spring is dry I might squeeze in a fourth. Yield I'm hoping for around 420 kg per mu — that's about what I got last two years.

**Maize (same 4 mu, right after wheat harvest):** This is the rushed part. Wheat comes off maybe June 5th or so, and I need maize in the ground within a week or the growing season gets too short. I can't do much tillage — just rotary till and go. I'll hire the village machinery operator to plant; doing it by hand for four mu in that window is too much. Hybrid seed, I buy it from the same shop. I apply a bag of compound fertilizer as base when planting, then topdress urea when the plants are knee-high, probably late July. Maize doesn't need as much irrigation — if the summer rains are normal, maybe once or twice. Yield around 480 kg per mu, maybe better if we get good rain in August.

**Cotton (3 mu):** I plant late April after the last frost risk. Cotton takes more work than anything — thinning, pest scouting, pinching the tops, multiple picks. I spray more pesticide on cotton than on grain crops, mainly for bollworm and aphids in summer. I split the fertilizer three ways: base fertilizer before planting, another application when bolls are forming, and sometimes a light topdress if the plants look tired. Irrigation twice, maybe three times if July is hot and dry. I expect about 260 kg of lint per mu. Picking starts September and goes into October. I'll hire three or four workers for the picking days — can't avoid it.

**Money worry:** Total I'm thinking around 4,500 yuan in cash for inputs this year. That's tight. If cotton prices fall again like two years ago I'll think hard about whether to keep that cotton ground. But not yet.
